newsitem.title: USA: Connecticut airport posts sharp cargo rise - report.
newsitem.headline: Connecticut airport posts sharp cargo rise - report.

text.p: Air cargo traffic at Bradley International Airport in Connecticut rose 13.5 percent in 1996, the biggest gain of New England's major airports, Hartford Courant reported Tuesday.
A summary by the Regional Air Cargo Review showed that Bradley handled 261 million pounds of cargo in 1996, some 31 million pounds more than it did in 1995, the report said.
Air cargo traffic at Bradley grew 25.2 percent in the first quarter of this year.

"The ease of getting into and out of the airport, the fact that it has been open 99.9 percent of the time, and the freight security and lack of pilfering at Bradley are among the main reasons why air cargo carriers are increasing use of the airport," Robert Juliano, chief of the transportation department's Bureau of Aviation and Ports, was quoted as saying.
Bradley lies between Hartford, Conn., and Springfield, Mass.
